subject: Acme — multi-year prepay: invoice phasing & seller-credit coordination
messages:
From: Lisa Guerrero <lisa.guerrero@acme.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme: multi-year prepay proposal — request for invoice split

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the proposal you shared on the demo. Procurement is ready to move forward with a 3-year prepay commitment but we need the invoices split to align with our fiscal year close. Specifically:

- Year 1 (FY2027): $1,200,000 — invoice delivered Q4 FY2027 (we need it recognized in FY2027)
- Year 2 (FY2028): $900,000 — invoice may be dated Jan 3, 2028 or invoiced in FY2027 but recognized in FY2028 depending on Redwood policy
- Year 3 (FY2029): $600,000

Can Redwood issue separate invoices that map to our year buckets or provide an accounting-friendly schedule / statement of work (SOW) that our finance team can use for rev-rec? Also please include any available seller credits to offset Year 2 ramp risk.

I've attached our PO and a short note on fiscal dates.

Attachments: ACME_PO_20270110.pdf

Best,
Lisa Guerrero
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Guerrero <lisa.guerrero@acme.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme: multi-year prepay proposal — request for invoice split

Hi Lisa — thanks, and great to hear procurement is ready.

High-level: we can absolutely support split invoicing and produce an amended SOW with explicit invoice schedule. To make sure we align with our revenue recognition and compliance requirements, looping in our finance lead Marcus and Sales Ops Stephanie. Two quick clarifying requests from our side:

1) Do you require separate legally-signed invoices per fiscal year, or is a single prepay invoice with copy-to-year ledgers acceptable?
2) For the seller credit you mentioned: are you expecting a dollar credit applied as an invoice reduction in Year 2, or an ongoing capacity credit (i.e., prepaid $ applied against usage)?

I've attached a proposed invoice split worksheet that outlines three options (yearly invoice issuance, single upfront invoice with internal ledger splits, and an amortized billing with credit note). Please review and we'll draft the amended SOW and DocuSign envelope once we agree.

Attachments: proposed_invoice_schedule.xlsx

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm rev-rec implications for each option (short note is fine). Stephanie, if we can commit to a modest seller credit, can you propose terms we can offer?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme: multi-year prepay proposal — request for invoice split

Markus / Stephanie — quick finance perspective. I reviewed Acme's PO and the three split options in the worksheet. Summary below (high level, for legal/controllership review):

Option A — Separate invoices dated in each fiscal year (preferred by Acme):
- We can issue one invoice per year with corresponding revenue recognized in that fiscal year provided services are commensurate with the period covered and collectability is established.
- Practical: Year 1 invoice issued Q4 FY2027 for FY2027 recognition; Year 2 invoice dated Jan 3, 2028 for FY2028, etc.
- Caveat: We will need to ensure there is contractual language tying payment timing to the service period (SOW exhibit).

Option B — Single upfront invoice with internal ledger allocation (Redwood invoices once, but provides accounting schedule for Acme):
- We can issue a single invoice at signing and provide a detailed allocation schedule to support Acme's rev-rec front/back allocation. Redwood would recognize revenue per our ASC 606 policy: we generally recognize revenue as service is delivered, so we'd amortize revenue across the service period.
- This approach is easy operationally but requires Acme's finance to accept allocation schedule for their side.

Option C — Upfront invoice + credit notes applied in later periods (seller credit):
- We can issue the upfront invoice for the full committed amount and then issue credit notes for Year 2/3 to reflect negotiated seller credits. Credits reduce revenue in the period the credit applies unless documented otherwise.

Key action items for paperwork:
- Draft SOW appendix with explicit invoice dates, service periods, and tax wording.
- If Acme requires revenue to be recognized in FY2027 for Year 1, we need Year 1 invoice dated and delivered before their FY2027 close (you noted Q4).
- For audit trail: attach internal revrec guidance (see attached).

Atts: revrec_guidance.pdf

I recommend Option A if Acme insists on per-year recognition tied to their fiscal close. Option B is fine if they prefer administrative simplicity.

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Accounting
Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Guerrero <lisa.guerrero@acme.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme: multi-year prepay proposal — request for invoice split

Hi Lisa — great to connect. Following Marcus's guidance, Redwood is prepared to accommodate a per-year invoice schedule (Option A) with the following commercial adjustment to help with your Year 2 ramp:

Proposal (commercial):
- Apply a 5% seller credit (one-time) on the Year 2 invoice amount, delivered as a credit note issued at Redwood's discretion to be applied against Year 2 usage.
- We will show the credit as a separate line item on the Year 2 invoice.
- If Acme prefers the credit applied as a reduction on the Year 1 invoice, we can accommodate, but tax/rev-rec treatment may differ. Finance, please flag any tax consequences.

Operational asks from Acme:
- Confirm that Year 1 invoice needs to be delivered by Feb 5, 2027 to meet your FY2027 close — we can commit to that if SOW is signed by Jan 25.
- Confirm the exact legal entity name and billing address to appear on invoices.

I will draft the amended SOW (invoice schedule + credit clause) and prepare a DocuSign envelope once we confirm the billing details. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2027-01 (FYI).

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Lisa Guerrero <lisa.guerrero@acme.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 20 Jan 2027 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme: multi-year prepay proposal — request for invoice split

Stephanie / Markus — thank you, that path works for Acme. We accept the 5% seller credit applied to Year 2 as a credit note. Confirming:

- Redwood will issue Year 1 invoice (for $1.2M) with delivery to Acme before Feb 5, 2027.
- Year 2 invoice will reflect a 5% credit on the $900k line (credit note issued and referenced on the invoice).
- Please ensure the amended SOW includes the invoice dates, service periods, and language that the credit is a one-time seller credit tied to this agreement.

Please send the amended SOW and DocuSign link for signature. Tax and remittance details: Acme Corp, 123 Industrial Way, Tax ID: 12-3456789.

Attachments requested: amended_sow_draft.docx

Best,
Lisa Guerrero
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation
